summary: Verified on the prepared gfx950 checkout that the no-rope MLA DCP writer used raw virtual locations while the rope writer localized them. Localized no-rope writes by DCP owner/rank, sized replicated DSA index-K storage for the target allocator's virtual location space (without double-scaling draft pools), and scaled the prefix-sharing capacity assertion for DCP virtual locations.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before numerical regression on gfx950: both DCP ranks wrote raw virtual rows instead of owner-local loc//world_size rows. Raw output: reports/j-7d79d9f95401/failing-before-norope.log
Passing-after GPU numerical comparison for no-rope and rope writes, DCP ranks 0 and 1, including owned and non-owned virtual locations. Raw output: reports/j-7d79d9f95401/passing-after-dcp-write.log

Index-K sizing boundaries: DCP target expands to virtual capacity, replicated draft avoids double scaling, and non-DCP retains the default. Raw output: reports/j-7d79d9f95401/passing-index-capacity.log

gpu_execution.evidence: The Triton regression compiled and executed on the assigned AMD gfx950 GPU; hardware evidence is retained in reports/j-7d79d9f95401/gpu.txt.

remaining_limitations: The reported GLM-5.3-Flash weights were unavailable, so no full-model semantic-quality or long-context watermark reproduction was performed.
Only one gfx950 GPU was assigned; the reported eight-rank H100 DCP server and multi-node behavior were not reproduced.
The sparse decode/verify LSE merge and sparse-extend all-gather paths were not qualified end to end by this fixture.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
ruff was unavailable in the prepared interpreter; focused pytest checks and git diff --check were used instead.
